units.function: Pure planning tests for reconciling history from a nested database worktree into a target company: Work, comments, Projects/workspaces, documents/revisions and attachments with preview identifiers, mappings and recorded adjustments.
units.dependencyDirection: The Vitest suite imports a pure merge planner/scope parser and supplies database-shaped records as in-memory fixtures. It verifies plans/counts only; no database transaction, asset copy, filesystem/Git operation or authorization is executed.
units.keyDataModels: Issue/Work identity and status/assignee/project/goal/execution links; comment authors; Project and local/remote workspace metadata; linked documents and numbered revisions; attachment asset/provider/object key/hash/author; project mapping/import overrides and adjustment counters.
units.lifecycle: Select merge scopes; deduplicate preserved UUIDs; assign new display identifiers; clear/map/import missing references and coerce invalid in-progress Work; merge comments; map/import Projects/workspaces; merge document histories and renumber conflicts; import attachments while clearing unresolved links; produce counts and adjustment plan.
units.testAssessment: Focused Vitest passed 8/8 tests on 2026-08-19 and CLI no-emit TypeScript passed. It thoroughly specifies several deterministic merge cases and adjustment counts, but omits apply/rollback, conflict policies for changed same-UUID records, cycles, tenant mismatch, concurrent target writes, asset-byte integrity, workspace path safety, huge histories, responsibility preservation and property/idempotency tests.
units.designRationale: Allow parallel local/nested worktree databases to contribute useful operational history back to a main instance without duplicating preserved entities or failing entirely when target references differ.
units.companyOsProblem: Hybrid/self-hosted Company OS must reconcile offline/local execution-node events and FDE configuration branches into an authoritative control plane without losing identity, responsibility, evidence, ordering or tenant boundaries.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT pure previewable deterministic planning, explicit mapping/import choices, adjustment accounting and preserved opaque source IDs. Redesign synchronization around immutable source event/evidence IDs, replica/node identity, causal/version vectors or server revisions, signed manifests and durable apply receipts. Preserve unresolved/deleted principal tombstones and original document revision identity instead of erasing responsibility or rewriting history semantics.
units.responsibilityConflict: Clearing missing author/assignee Agent references destroys who performed or owned historical actions. Importing Work without its responsible human/contract/data/approval chain and renumbering revisions can make the merged record look locally authoritative when provenance is incomplete.

securityFindings: Missing Agent authors are deliberately cleared from comments/attachments; this prevents dangling foreign keys but erases attribution and is unacceptable for responsibility/evidence without a preserved source-principal tombstone.
Document revision conflicts are renumbered in the target; original revision number, branch/node identity, parentage and content digest need preservation to prevent history ambiguity or substitution.

Source Project workspaces include absolute cwd, repository URL and setup/cleanup-capable metadata; importing them can leak topology or enable unsafe execution unless sanitized/rebound per target node.
Attachment plans rely on objectKey/provider/hash metadata fixtures but do not verify bytes, source authorization, malware/content policy, cross-tenant storage namespace or copy atomicity.
Same-UUID changed entities appear treated as existing/deduplicated in covered cases; divergent content conflict detection and malicious UUID collision are untested.
Preview issue identifiers depend on a counter start, but concurrent target inserts and apply-time reservation/fencing are not tested.
Company id is supplied to the planner; all source rows' tenant consistency and target authorization are not tested.
No size/depth/cycle limits or streaming strategy are tested for large graphs/histories, creating memory and denial-of-service risk.
